responses.sql: SELECT AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(replacement_cost / rental_rate) AS avg_cost_to_rate_ratio FROM film WHERE length >= 112

assumptions.assumption: A 'long film' is one with length at or above 112 minutes (inclusive cutoff), since the request says 'using 112 minutes as the cutoff' without stating whether 112 itself counts.
Films with NULL length are excluded by the filter; rental_rate is NOT NULL and never 0 (values 0.99, 2.99, 4.99), so the per-film division is safe.

alternatives.interpretation: Long films are strictly longer than 112 minutes (exclusive cutoff).

responses.sql: SELECT AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(replacement_cost / NULLIF(rental_rate, 0)) AS avg_cost_to_rate_ratio FROM film WHERE length >= 112

assumptions.assumption: A long film is one with length at least 112 minutes (length >= 112), so films of exactly 112 minutes are included. Films with NULL length are excluded.
The ratio is computed per film and then averaged. rental_rate is never 0 (values are 0.99, 2.99 and 4.99), and NULLIF only guards against division by zero.

alternatives.interpretation: A long film is strictly longer than 112 minutes (length > 112), so films of exactly 112 minutes are excluded.

assumptions.assumption: A long film is one with length >= 112 minutes, so the cutoff itself counts as long. The request says 'using 112 as the cutoff' but doesn't say whether the cutoff value is included.
The ratio is computed per film and then averaged. AVG ignores NULLs. rental_rate is NOT NULL and at least 0.99, so there is no division by zero. If no film qualifies, both values come back NULL.
